title: Rethinking Team Member Rewards
author: Admired Leadership
summary: The post argues that leaders fall into a rut, relying on the same handful of rewards: pay, public awards, flexibility, development, and travel. These are appreciated but lose value through repetition. The author recommends discovering what team members truly care about outside work, such as their children, health, pets, and homes, and rewarding along those lines with things like tutoring, wellness programs, or workspace upgrades. Because these rewards are unexpected and personal, they underline appreciation more strongly and build trust.
points: Repeating the same few rewards dilutes their impact.
Effective rewards connect to what individuals value away from work.
Examples include tutoring for children, wellness programs, pet grooming, certifications, and charitable giving.
Unexpected, personalized recognition builds the trust and good feelings that bind teams.
quotes: When it comes to rewarding team members for exceptional work and results, leaders are often in a rut. They rely on the same four or five rewards to recognize people.
While these mainstays are appreciated by team members, going to the well for the same rewards over and over lessens their value.
By exploring what makes people feel differently about themselves and what they hold in the highest regard, leaders can find rewards that stand apart and underline appreciation.
Just ask yourself where team members invest their time and resources away from the workplace, and what they hold dear.
Rewards that focus on what matters most to people, besides compensation, can boost motivation and foster a positive and supportive environment in a way that traditional rewards can’t.
